suite.texte: Age doesn't tell you whether you're made for each other. The love compatibility test looks at your values, your wishes and your plans, in twenty questions.

section1.title: How do you calculate the age gap in a couple?
section1.p1: To calculate the age difference between two people, you just count the time between their two dates of birth. For example, if one was born on March 12, 1994 and the other on July 3, 1997, the gap is 3 years, 3 months and 21 days.
section1.p2: Sounds simple, but there's a little detail that often surprises people: the gap "in years" changes during the year. With the example above, between March 12 and July 2, the older one has already had their birthday and the other hasn't, so your two ages are 4 years apart. The rest of the year, 3 years. The tool above tells you on which dates it switches for you.
section1.p3: It also adds the half-your-age-plus-seven rule and the date when your two ages will add up to 100. And for a more playful calculation, there's also the love calculator, where two first names are enough!

section2.title: What is the half-your-age-plus-seven rule?
section2.p1: It's a rule you hear a lot in English-speaking countries. You take the age of the older person, divide it by two and add seven: that gives the youngest acceptable age for the other, according to the rule. For example, at 30 the limit is 22, at 40 it's 27, and at 50 it's 32.
section2.p2: It's not new: it already shows up at the turn of the 20th century in a book by Max O'Rell, a French writer who wrote a lot about the English. Of course, there's nothing scientific about it. It's more a way of saying "beyond that, people will talk".
section2.p3: The funny thing is that it gets looser over time. With a 10-year gap, the rule is only met once the younger one is 24 and the older one 34. In real life, people often accept wider gaps: in a study of 21,245 people by two German researchers, Sascha Schwarz and Manfred Hassebrauck, men accepted on average a partner up to 10 years younger and 4.5 years older, and women a partner up to 8 years older and 5 years younger. In a famous study across 37 cultures, psychologist David Buss found the same pattern everywhere: men preferred younger partners, women older ones.

section3.title: Is a big age gap a problem in a relationship?
section3.p1: Most of the time, it isn't the gap itself that causes trouble, it's what it changes in everyday life. With 3 years between you, you have the same school memories and the same songs. With 15, one of you may already be thinking about retirement while the other is starting a career.
section3.p2: Research doesn't settle it. A study from Emory University in the US, of about 3,000 married people, found a higher risk of divorce as the gap grows: about 18% more with a 5-year gap and 39% more with a 10-year gap. But its authors admit it may not be the gap itself, rather the kind of couples who have big gaps. In the UK, a 2003 study by the Office for National Statistics also found more divorces as the gap grew, whichever partner was older, while a 2008 study concluded the age gap was no real risk to a marriage.
section3.p3: What matters most are the topics the gap makes more pressing:
points: Kids: whether you want them, when, how many. With a big gap, the question comes sooner for one of you, and being ready to become parents is something to check together.
Pace of life: going out, friends, weekend energy. It's not about age but about what you want, and that can be compared.
What others think: family, friends, jokes. It sometimes weighs more than the gap itself, and it's better to talk about it together than to suffer through it on your own.
The future: retirement, health, who will look after whom. Not very romantic, but talking about it early avoids bad surprises.
section3.apres: In the end, whether your values and your plans match counts far more than the years on your ID cards.

section4.title: What is the average age gap in a couple?
section4.p1: In the US, about a third of married couples (33.9%) are within two years of each other, according to the Census Bureau's 2017 figures. The husband is two to three years older in 19.6% of couples and the wife in 6.9%; with six to nine years, it's 11.2% for husbands against 2.8% for wives.
section4.p2: On average, the gap is about two and a half years in the US and about three years in the UK. And couples where the woman is older are less rare than they used to be: in England and Wales, the share of women marrying a younger man rose from 15% in 1963 to 26% in 1998.
section4.p3: Same-sex couples tend to have wider gaps. In 2023, the Census Bureau found that 24% of same-sex couples were within two years of each other, against 35% of opposite-sex couples.

faq.title: Your questions about age gaps in couples
faq.q1: What is the ideal age gap in a relationship?
faq.a1: There isn't one. What matters is wanting the same things and having plans that go in the same direction. For the record, the average gap is about two and a half years in the US.
faq.q2: How do you calculate an age gap?
faq.a2: Count the time between the two dates of birth: full years first, then months, then days. The tool at the top of the page does it to the day, and also tells you during which part of the year your gap "in years" goes up by one.
faq.q3: How does the half-your-age-plus-seven rule work?
faq.a3: Divide the older person's age by two and add seven: that's the youngest acceptable age for the other, according to the rule. At 36, that gives 25. It's a popular rule of thumb, not a scientific one.
faq.q4: Is a 10-year age gap a lot?
faq.a4: It's less common than people think: in the US, even a gap of six to nine years with an older husband only concerns 11.2% of married couples (2017). That doesn't stop a couple from working, what you want and plan together matters most.
faq.q5: Is it rare for the woman to be older?
faq.a5: Less and less. In the US, the wife is two to three years older in 6.9% of married couples and six to nine years older in 2.8% (2017). In England and Wales, the share of women marrying a younger man went from 15% to 26% between 1963 and 1998.
faq.q6: Are our dates of birth saved anywhere?
faq.a6: No. They stay in your browser, on your phone or computer, so the result shows up when you come back. Nothing is sent to a server.
